_notes: THE CONTACT BURST, ALONE -- the second quarter of the old combined recipe.
EXPLICIT RECTS, NOT A FLOOR-DIVIDED GRID, and this is the correction the combined
recipe's own notes declined to make. water_contact_8f.png is 1774x887 over 4x2;
neither divides. The sources' README states the column edges 0, 444, 887, 1331,
1774 and the row edges 0, 444, 887 -- 444/443 alternating. A floor grid takes 443
everywhere, and the cost is not one lost pixel per cell: by the fourth column it
starts two pixels LEFT of where the cell does, so a sheet whose art reaches its
seams slices a sliver of the neighbour in. Measured on this sheet, five of the
eight cells' content bboxes touch a cell edge, so the seams are exactly where the
ink is. The rects are the README's own numbers.
CANVAS 512, WHICH IS HEADROOM RATHER THAN TIDINESS. The scale steps below grow a
cell about its own centre INSIDE its own bounds and then feather the outer ring,
so 1.06 applied to a crown already filling 425 of a 444 cell is not 6% bigger --
it is 6% bigger with 3px shaved off each side and a 12px fade welded to what is
left. The combined recipe never met this because its shared canvas was the core's
512 and the contact cells arrived padded into it; split per layer, this recipe's
own largest cell IS 444 and that headroom left with the core. So it is stated.
contact_f0 KEEPS ITS 1.10, THOUGH THE PILOT DOES NOT PLAY IT. The scale was a
measured bridge between two sheets in ONE sequence -- core_f5's content bbox is
454x472 of 512 against contact_f0's 425x417 of 444, so the ball visibly shrank
for one frame at the join. Split, the core and the splash are separate layers
with separate boxes (190 and 300 units), so there is no join left to correct; and
the splash layer authors startFrame 2, which skips this frame for the reason the
brief gives -- contact frame 1 contains an APPROACHING ball, and replaying an
approach after arrival is a second impact time. The frame stays in the folder,
corrected, so the choice is an authored number rather than a deleted asset.
contact_f3 IS THE PEAK and gets hold: 2, the second 6% larger -- 27% ink coverage
against the runner-up's 23%, and the widest crown in the sheet. One frame reads
as a drawing going past; two growing into each other reads as a blow landing. The
same trick frost_flare and mud_burst already use.
Nine frames out of eight cells. The splash layer plays eight of them at 26fps
from startFrame 2, which is 0.308s of compression, crown, breakup and a clearing
centre.
